name: Celeste Landry

summary.text: Celeste Landry is a longtime volunteer lobbyist with the League of Women Voters and an advocate for alternative voting methods, running as the Forward Party nominee for Colorado Secretary of State.
She has lived in Colorado and voted in every election since 1994 and describes herself as a nationally recognized expert on better voting methods.

experience.text: Volunteer lobbyist at the Colorado Capitol, the Title Board, and Secretary of State rulemaking hearings on election and voting-method issues.
Says she introduced U.S. Rep. Joe Neguse to the federal Fair Representation Act, which he has since co-sponsored each session.

positions.source_title: Colorado Secretary of State candidate Q&A
positions.quote: In general, we can be proud of Colorado's system; it is excellent at balancing access to voting with election security.
positions.note: A separate questionnaire has her calling Colorado's system 'gold-standard' while also proposing to further limit electronic ballot return, a narrower issue distinct from mail ballots themselves.

research_notes: No endorsements found on a fetched page. Her questionnaire answer criticizing federal CISA changes under the Trump administration was close to challenge-federal-policies but was about election-security coordination specifically, not a general stance on suing the administration, so it was left unsourced rather than stretched. Mail-ballot-id, plain-language-ballots and redistricting-commission are unsourced; her Ballotpedia survey (submitted February 23, 2026) and campaign focus on proportional/ranked voting methods rather than these specific measures. Second pass 2026-10-14: fetched her campaign site's Priorities page (celeste4sos.com/priorities), which details her support for proportional and ranked/approval voting methods and paper-ballot audits; it reinforces keep-mail-voting but does not address Amendment 85's plain-language requirement, Amendment 86's redistricting commission, or lawsuits against the federal administration specifically enough to code without stretching. No new positions were added.
